title: Amazon Expands Its Drone Delivery Service
paragraphs: Amazon plans to greatly expand its drone delivery service in the United States, bringing it to nearly 500 cities and towns by the end of 2026.

The company announced the plan on August 19. Its drone delivery service, called Prime Air, currently operates from 11 sites in seven states: Arizona, Florida, Kansas, Louisiana, Michigan, Nebraska and Texas. The expansion would make the service about six times larger.

Amazon said it plans to launch drone delivery in several new metropolitan areas, including Chicago, Atlanta, Cleveland, Syracuse in New York, and Boise in Idaho. More communities are expected to be added later in the year.

However, the number may sound larger than it really is. The figure of nearly 500 includes every city and town within the area that each drone site can reach. Each site covers about 175 square miles, so one site can serve many small communities. This means Amazon is not planning to build 500 new drone bases. The company has not said exactly how many new sites it will open.

Prime Air uses a drone called the MK30, which can carry packages weighing up to 5 pounds. According to reports, delivery is free for Prime members who spend $50 or more. Smaller orders cost $2.99 for Prime members, and $4.99 for customers who are not members.

The expansion also depends on approval from government regulators. Drone flights in the US are controlled by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), and some of the new sites will need its permission before they can start operating. According to one report, the launch in the Syracuse area could be delayed until 2027.
Even so, the plan shows that Amazon believes drones will become a bigger part of how people receive their online orders.
